The main takeaway from our work is that
quantum automata, as well as quantum Turing machines, can be employed to simulate quantum spin-networks and, in particular, to compute the colored Jones polynomial of a link at any root of unity.
quantum automata can be used to simulate the dynamics of the Chern-Simmons theory, which in turn can be exploited to compute topological invariants such as the Jones polynomials of links.
the spin-network quantum simulator is a powerful tool for computing link polynomials, which are the basic building blocks for knot theory and low dimensional topology.
